result.summary: The intersection is equipped with marked zebra crosswalks and pedestrian signals, providing basic infrastructure for crossing. However, the wide roadway increases pedestrian exposure time, and old rails embedded in the brick pavement create a potential tripping hazard.

hazards.name: Embedded Rails
hazards.description: Disused trolley tracks embedded in the brick pavement present a tripping hazard and can be slippery when wet.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground pavement area within the intersection

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to vehicle traffic without a refuge.

hazards.name: Sight Line Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb near the intersection may block visibility between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the curb line

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pavement Remediation
interventions.description: Remove or fill the unused rails to create a smooth, level walking surface for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection corners to ensure clear sight lines for all road users.

result.summary: The intersection features a marked zebra crosswalk and overhead traffic signals within an industrial setting. Pedestrian safety is compromised by embedded rail tracks in the roadway and the absence of visible pedestrian-specific signal heads.

hazards.name: Embedded Rail Tracks
hazards.description: The presence of rail tracks and uneven brick paving in the crosswalk area creates a significant trip hazard for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible, leaving pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve crossing safety and clarity.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and increase the visibility of pedestrians to approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Level Crossing Surface
interventions.description: Repair and level the pavement around the rail tracks to eliminate trip hazards within the crosswalk.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalk markings and overhead traffic signals within an industrial/commercial corridor. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the wide roadway lacks pedestrian refuge islands or visible dedicated pedestrian signal heads, increasing exposure for those crossing.

hazards.name: Long unprotected crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the entire width of the roadway without a median refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No visible pedestrian-specific signal heads are present to provide clear crossing intervals.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time, reducing exposure.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to improve predictability and safety at the crossing.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban street with a marked continental crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. The environment is characterized by commercial and industrial buildings, trolley tracks embedded in the pavement, and a lack of physical pedestrian protection such as medians or curb extensions.
